title: Ordinary derived adjunction of a simplicial Quillen pair
statement: Use model categories, weak factorization systems, functorial factorizations, cofibrant and fibrant objects as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], simplicial tensors and cotensors as defined in [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], and the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Enlarge universes so the categories and localizations below exist as ordinary categories. A simplicial model category means a model category enriched, tensored and cotensored over simplicial sets, in which for each cofibration $a:A\to B$ and fibration $p:X\to Y$ the corner map $\operatorname{Map}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$ is a Kan fibration, trivial if $a$ or $p$ is weak. Let $\mathcal M,\mathcal N$ be simplicial model categories and let $L:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:U$ be an enriched adjunction, meaning natural isomorphisms of mapping simplicial sets. Assume $L$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, equivalently $U$ preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. For each model category let $q$ denote its ordinary finite-string localization at weak equivalences. Choose functorial cofibrant replacements $QX\to X$ and fibrant replacements $Y\to RY$. Assume the natural mapping-component comparisons of [lem-coef-simplicial-mapping-localization] for both categories. Then $LQ$ and $UR$, followed by localization, invert weak equivalences and induce ordinary functors $\mathbf LL:\mathcal M[W^{-1}]\rightleftarrows\mathcal N[W^{-1}]:\mathbf RU$. They are adjoint. For cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $Y$, the adjunction bijection is the composite $\operatorname{Hom}(qLP,qY)\cong\pi_0\operatorname{Map}(LP,Y)\cong\pi_0\operatorname{Map}(P,UY)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(qP,qUY)$; in particular it sends every actual map to its ordinary adjunct. For arbitrary objects the unit is represented by $QX\to ULQX\to URLQX$ with $q(QX\to X)$ inverted, and the counit by $LQURY\to LURY\to RY$ with $q(Y\to RY)$ inverted. These maps are natural and satisfy the triangle identities. If $L$ or $U$ already preserves all weak equivalences, its derived functor agrees naturally with its direct localization.

source.place: Paragraph 2, coherent coefficient adjunction; agent-written ordinary prerequisite extracted from original lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus proof Step 15. Second paragraph: Brown preservation and the natural component Hom bijections descend through finite strings to the ordinary derived adjunction, with replacement unit and counit. No Stacks tag is asserted for this homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Write $c_X:QX\to X$ and $r_Y:Y\to RY$ for the functorial replacements, $q_{\mathcal M},q_{\mathcal N}$ for localization, and $\eta,\epsilon$ for the original adjunction maps. The model conventions are [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. Since $L$ is a left adjoint, it preserves the initial object: maps out of its image are uniquely identified by adjunction with maps out of the initial object. Thus preservation of cofibrations makes $LP$ cofibrant whenever $P$ is. The two forms of the Quillen hypothesis agree: by the adjunction, lifting problems of $L(i)$ against $p$ correspond bijectively to lifting problems of $i$ against $U(p)$, and in each weak factorization system each class is exactly the maps with the lifting property against the other. Hence $L$ preserves cofibrations (respectively trivial cofibrations) if and only if $U$ preserves trivial fibrations (respectively fibrations). Dually $UY$ is fibrant whenever $Y$ is fibrant. These observations check the object hypotheses needed for the mapping-component comparisons below.

source.place: Paragraph 2, ordinary coefficient-adjunction prerequisite: cofibrant and fibrant hypotheses

proof.text: For a weak equivalence $f:X\to X'$ between cofibrant objects, [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] gives $f=pi$ with $i,s$ cofibrations, $p$ a trivial fibration, and $ps=1$. Two-out-of-three applied to $pi=f$ and $ps=1$ makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. Hence $L(i),L(s)$ are weak; $L(p)L(s)=1$ makes $L(p)$ weak, so $L(f)$ is weak. Dually for a weak equivalence between fibrant objects the same node gives $f=pi$, $i$ trivial, $p,r$ fibrations and $ri=1$. Two-out-of-three makes $p,r$ trivial fibrations. Thus $U(p),U(r)$ are weak, $U(r)U(i)=1$ makes $U(i)$ weak, and $U(f)$ is weak.

For a weak equivalence $f:X\to X'$, $c_{X'}Qf=fc_X$ implies by two-out-of-three that $Qf$ is weak. Dually $Rf$ is weak. Step 2 therefore makes $LQf$ and $URf$ weak. Define $F(q_{\mathcal M}X)=q_{\mathcal N}LQX$ and $G(q_{\mathcal N}Y)=q_{\mathcal M}URY$; on ordinary arrows use $q_{\mathcal N}LQf$ and $q_{\mathcal M}URg$, and on a formal inverse use the inverse of this image. Identities, compositions and the two inverse relations are preserved, so evaluation of finite strings gives well-defined ordinary functors $F,G$ on the given localizations.

For cofibrant $P$ and fibrant $Y$, Step 1 makes $LP$ cofibrant and $UY$ fibrant. The statement [lem-coef-simplicial-mapping-localization] and the given enriched adjunction yield the bijection
$$B_{P,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}(q_{\mathcal N}LP,q_{\mathcal N}Y)\ \cong\ \pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal N}(LP,Y)\ \cong\ \pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}(P,UY)\ \cong\ \operatorname{Hom}(q_{\mathcal M}P,q_{\mathcal M}UY).$$
The cited node states that the outside maps are induced by actual localization and natural for actual arrows between cofibrant sources and fibrant targets. The middle isomorphism is enriched natural by hypothesis. Hence $B$ is natural for these arrows and sends $q(f)$ to $q(f^\sharp)$ for every actual $f:LP\to Y$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, ordinary prerequisite: natural component Hom bijections

proof.text:
For arbitrary $X,Y$, define the bijection $\Phi_{X,Y}:\operatorname{Hom}(FX,q_{\mathcal N}Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}(q_{\mathcal M}X,GY)$ by
$$\Phi_{X,Y}(a)=B_{QX,RY}(q_{\mathcal N}(r_Y)\circ a)\circ q_{\mathcal M}(c_X)^{-1}.$$
Both replacements are weak, so the composition maps here are bijective, and Step 4 applies to $QX,RY$. For an actual $f:X'\to X$, naturality of $B$ for $Qf$ and $c_XQf=fc_{X'}$ give
$$\Phi_{X',Y}(a\circ F(qf))=\Phi_{X,Y}(a)\circ qf.$$
For actual $g:Y\to Y'$, use $Rg\,r_Y=r_{Y'}g$ and naturality of $B$ for $Rg$ to get
$$\Phi_{X,Y'}(qg\circ a)=G(qg)\circ\Phi_{X,Y}(a).$$
For a weak $f$ or $g$ these equalities also hold for its formal inverse, by multiplying the equality on the relevant side by the inverse images (which Step 3 made invertible). Induction on the length of a composable string proves both naturality laws for every localization arrow. This does not require a stronger bifibrant comparison. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to $\Phi$ to obtain $F\dashv G$, with unit $\Phi(1)$, counit $\Phi^{-1}(1)$, naturality and triangle identities.

source.place: Paragraph 2, ordinary prerequisite: Hom bijections descend through finite strings

proof.text:
For cofibrant $P$, $c_P:QP\to P$ is a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects, so Step 2 makes $L(c_P)$ weak. For fibrant $Y$, $r_Y:Y\to RY$ is weak between fibrant objects, so $U(r_Y)$ is weak. These give the identifications $FP\cong qLP$ and $GY\cong qUY$. For $a:qLP\to qY$, naturality of $B$ gives
$$\Phi_{P,Y}(a\circ qL(c_P))=qU(r_Y)\circ B_{P,Y}(a).$$
Indeed its defining expression is $B_{QP,RY}(qr_Y\circ a\circ qL(c_P))\circ qc_P^{-1}$; naturality first moves $c_P$ and $r_Y$ outside $B$, and $qc_P\circ qc_P^{-1}=1$ cancels. Thus under precisely these replacement identifications the adjunction bijection is the composite asserted in the statement, including its value on actual maps.

source.place: Paragraph 2, ordinary prerequisite: comparison on cofibrant-fibrant objects

proof.text:
Compute the unit by applying Step 5 to $a=1_{qLQX}$, with target $LQX$. By Step 4 the actual map $r_{LQX}:LQX\to RLQX$ has adjunct $U(r_{LQX})\eta_{QX}$. Hence the unit is
$$qX\xrightarrow{qc_X^{-1}}qQX\xrightarrow{q\eta_{QX}}qULQX\xrightarrow{qU(r_{LQX})}qURLQX.$$
Here the arrow $ULQX\to URLQX$ is $U$ of the replacement in $\mathcal N$. For the counit, use $X=URY$ in Step 5 and solve $\Phi(a)=1_{qURY}$. The equation is $B_{QURY,RY}(qr_Y\circ a)=qc_{URY}$. The actual adjunct of $c_{URY}:QURY\to URY$ is $\epsilon_{RY}\circ L(c_{URY})$, so
$$a=(qr_Y)^{-1}\circ q\epsilon_{RY}\circ qL(c_{URY}):qLQURY\to qY.$$
These are exactly the unit and counit words claimed. Since they were computed as $\Phi(1)$ and $\Phi^{-1}(1)$, Step 5 and [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] give their naturality and both triangle identities, without assuming replacement maps commute with $L$ or $U$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, ordinary prerequisite: replacement unit/counit and triangle identities

proof.text: If $L$ preserves all weak equivalences, define its direct localization $\overline L$ by evaluation on strings as in Step 3. The arrows $qL(c_X):FX\to\overline L(qX)$ are invertible and natural for ordinary arrows by naturality of $c$. The same equations for formal inverses follow by cancellation, and for strings by composition. They therefore give a natural isomorphism $F\cong\overline L$. Dually, if $U$ preserves all weak equivalences, $qU(r_Y):\overline U(qY)\to GY$ gives a natural isomorphism from its direct localization to $G$.
